title: Attaining the Negative Sign by a Coalition
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be monotone, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. There exists an input $y$ agreeing with $x$ outside $J$ and satisfying $f(y)=-1$ if and only if $f$ evaluated at the input obtained from $x$ by setting every coordinate in $J$ to $-1$ equals $-1$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$J$ is a finite set of coordinates among the $n$ coordinates
$x$ is an input in the sign cube
